problems.text:
The first decision of the brief no longer holds as written. The refix added a second threshold: the purge test now reads any growth up to 3 noise units of the column as `no-growth`, not only growth up to the plateau minimum. The brief says nothing else in `judge::purge` changes. `judge::combine` is textually unchanged, but a plateau with a retained purge over real growth is no longer inconclusive when that growth is inside 3 noise units. The refix report says itself that this goes beyond the brief.

Replay on prepared series, 200 seeds per shape, comparing HEAD, the tree, and the tree with the minimum alone:
- Real slow leaks now read non-leak. They were inconclusive at HEAD and with the minimum alone.
  - JVM, bound off-heap finding with os.rss as primary, 300 KB per point under a 5 MB scatter: non-leak in 5 of 200 before, 112 now (16+16 points); 60 to 158 (8+8). A bound non-leak leads to a refute.
  - Native program where os.rss decides alone, 30 KB per point under a 300 KB scatter: 6 to 119 (8+8), 0 to 23 (16+16).
  - Python, anonymous leak of 8 KB per point under a 60 KB scatter: 0 to 79 (6 with the minimum alone).
  - A probe count gauge gaining one entry every other point under a jitter of 8: 0 to 107. The brief wanted columns with no minimum unchanged.
- A file-backed leak below the noise of os.rss: os.rss now reads non-leak beside the leaking os.rss_file, so the overall verdict moves from leak to inconclusive in 20 of 200 seeds (Go, 16+16), 28 (Go, 8+8) and 124 (JVM, 8+8, 5 MB scatter). None reads non-leak.
- A released purge inside the floor becomes `no-growth`. One flat JVM seed moved from non-leak to leak, because the plateau test read growth-continues and the released purge no longer overrides it. Non-leak results also lose N-ALLOC or N-HEADROOM: in my go-gc-tuned-batch run os.rss stood 8.1 MB above the warm-up, the purge returned 26.8 MB, and the reading is `no-growth`.

What the floor buys: flat series stop reading inconclusive (flat native 106 of 200 to 1; flat Python 158 to 39 with the minimum, to 6 with the floor). In my python-report-memo-bounded run both unbound non-leak verdicts rest on it, with os.rss growth of 155.6 and 135.2 KB against a floor of 172 KB; a third reading of 188.4 KB was above it.

No test covers the leak side, and the VERIFY row and the reference state the rule but not this cost. Direction: decide it explicitly. Either take the noise limit out, which is the brief's rule and makes the flat Python run inconclusive more often (next item), or keep it as a named decision with a leak-side test and the cost written into the row and the reference.

The second problem of the first check is fixed the way its direction says, but its symptom remains: a flat Python run still reads inconclusive through os.rss.

The harness part holds. `before` is now the checkpoint's own reading, and both new harness tests fail with the HEAD agent (replayed in my scratch dir: `before` stood 1.7 and 3.5 MB above the own reading against a slack of 512 KB, and ctypes was absent at start-up, exit 3).

The symptom: 8 runs of the command-level scenario with the tree binary (python-report-memo-bounded, first trend edited so that only os.rss_file passes) gave 5 non-leak and 3 inconclusive. Each inconclusive came from os.rss voting with plateau and purge retained (growth 197 to 238 KB, drop -172 to -176 KB). The refix report says 1 of 8. With the minimum alone it would be 7 of 8, computed from the same readings.

Cause in the data: growth is read against the single warm-up point, and that point sits below every later point of the first series in three fixture runs (earlier run, first check, mine): 41 to 74 KB below the later minimum, 104 to 132 KB below the later mean. The trim returns nothing.

So the command-level test the brief asked for (overall verdict non-leak) cannot be asserted, and the test now asserts only that the verdict is not leak. The row and the report say this openly. Direction: an owner decision. Either accept it as open (the `corrected` of row 521 then covers os.rss_file only), or change what the purge growth is measured against for such a run.

The trim step still loads a module between its two readings: `import platform` and `platform.libc_ver()` run after `before` is taken. Measured in a bare interpreter with the tree agent: the import adds 164 kB of anonymous memory. In all 11 purge records of my runs (3 fixture, 8 command-level) os.rss `after` stood 160 to 176 KB above `before`; os.rss_file did not move. Every Python trim record therefore reports a drop that is short by that much, and a trim that returned up to that much reads retained. The harness test lets it through with its 512 KB slack. Direction: import platform in `_preload_trim` and tighten the slack.

The command-level test does not exercise what its comment describes. In all 8 runs the purge of os.rss_file read `no-growth` (growth -102 to +29 KB, drop 0), not retained, so the exemption is not what makes the column non-leak there. By the rule, the test passes with the exemption removed, and it passes with the old agent alone because the exemption then covers the reading. It fails only when both changes are gone. Each change is pinned by its own unit or harness test, so this is a gap in this one test plus a comment that describes another path.
Two overlong lines remain in the changed text: 132 and 152 characters where the neighbours wrap near 100. The report's "the reference lines are wrapped" holds for the purge paragraph only.

The new basis line is still inexact when the only passing columns are `jvm.nmt.*` categories (memory in use, neither a peak nor a size) or activity counters. No reader of the old text exists in crates, bench/runner, skills, agents, harness, docs or data.

Cost of the start-up preload: every measured Python process on Linux now runs `/sbin/ldconfig -p` (through `ctypes.util.find_library`) and imports 28 more modules, subprocess, tempfile and shutil among them (80 to 108). Start-up went from 54 to 86 ms per process here. tracemalloc and memray start after it, so py.traced is unaffected. `ctypes.CDLL("libc.so.6")` would avoid the child process.

My replay crate (own package name, built into the shared target) left these three unit directories, 93 MB together. Cargo's artifact listing shows only that crate uses them. I removed the linked binary `target/debug/n1b-replay` and its `.d` file. One slip: a `py_compile` check of the agent created `harness/python/__pycache__` (git-ignored) in the repository; I removed it at once, and `git status` shows nothing from me.

confirmed:
The refix does what the first check directed on all three problems, the tests pass and the three fixtures pass, but two problems remain: a noise limit added beyond the brief, and a flat Python run that is still inconclusive in 3 of my 8 runs.

**First-check items**
- Problem 1 (file-backed leak could read non-leak): fixed as directed.
  - `pick.rs` equals HEAD apart from the new list, the basis wording and one test; os.rss_file votes again.
  - Only its purge reading is dropped, and only when its plateau reads plateau (`alloc_cmd.rs:268-274`).
  - Replay: the file-leak shapes read as at HEAD and none reads non-leak in 800 seeded series. The leak-to-inconclusive shift is in problem 1 of my list.
- Problem 2 (Python trim read `before` after its import): harness fixed as directed; the symptom remains (problem 2 of my list).
- Problem 3 (false VERIFY sentence): fixed. Row 521 now says only python-graph-churn failed the earlier run.
- Minor 1 (per-kind statement): done in `pick.rs:42-50` and row 521. I checked that the Go and Node purge records carry no os.rss_file.
- Minor 2 (basis line): changed. Minor 3: the `NoGrowth` doc is done; the wrapping is partial.

**Claims of the refix report**
- Confirmed:
  - `pick.rs` reverted and the fallback block gone.
  - The exemption rule and its condition.
  - The cause and fix of the Python agent.
  - The command-level test no longer asserts the overall verdict.
  - The noise floor exists and goes beyond the brief.
  - Two rows rewritten, 4 cells each, no plan or model names, no measured byte counts (only the 32 KiB rule constant).
  - `combine` and `overall` have no changed line.
- Seen-failing claims, confirmed by replaying each test's exact series with one change removed at a time:
  - Go-shape test: retained and inconclusive at HEAD.
  - File stair test: inconclusive with the exemption off.
  - Scatter test: retained with the floor at the minimum.
  - Ordinary-column guard: inconclusive in every variant.
  - The growing-file test passes at HEAD and fails if the exemption ignored the plateau verdict.
  - The two judge-level tests and the pick test: by reading.
- False in part:
  - "The restored behaviour matches HEAD": not where os.rss votes beside os.rss_file (leak to inconclusive through the floor).
  - "The reference lines are wrapped": two overlong lines remain.
- Different here: "1 of 8" inconclusive; I got 3 of 8.

**Decisions and tests**
- Purge uses the plateau minimum: yes, plus the noise limit. `judge::combine` unchanged: yes.
- No test was skipped, ignored or weakened against HEAD. The diff removes no assertion, and the existing purge tests only gained the 0.0 argument.

**Runs here**
- `cargo test -j 2 --no-fail-fast -p dla-cli --test alloc_test`: 4 passed.
- Unit tests of the alloc code (`--bin dla alloc_cmd`): 70 passed.
- `cargo test -j 2 --no-fail-fast -p dla-workload --test harness_capture_python`: 16 passed.
- Workspace clippy with `-D warnings`: exit 0, from cache. `cargo fmt --all --check` clean. `dla schema --check` ok.

**Adversarial cases (HEAD against tree)**
1. File-backed leak below the noise of os.rss: never non-leak. Leak becomes inconclusive in 20, 28 and 124 of 200 seeds, depending on the shape.
2. Flat Python run with the trim purge:
   - With the new agent's record: non-leak, as at HEAD's judge.
   - With the old agent's record: still inconclusive through os.rss.
   - With 100 KB of early growth under a 60 KB scatter: inconclusive becomes non-leak, the intended cut.
   - With a quiet os.rss: stays inconclusive.
3. Go heap leak of 100 KB with a retained purge: identical to HEAD in all 1,600 seeded series.
   - Column reads leak 200 of 200 with a 6 KB scatter.
   - Growth only in the main window: inconclusive 200 of 200.
   - None reads non-leak.
   - Clean steps and concave fills kept by the purge (126 series): inconclusive in both.

A case that was inconclusive for a good reason and now reads non-leak: yes, slow real leaks under the scatter of the deciding column (problem 1).

**Fixtures** (copies of binaries built from this tree, `--parallel 1`; all three pass)

| Fixture | Now (refuted, confirmed, rule-out, leaks, passed columns) | Earlier run |
|---|---|---|
| python-report-memo-bounded | 4, 0, true, 0, 2 | 1, 0, true, 0, 2 |
| python-graph-churn | 2, 0, true, 0, 2 | 0, 0, false, 0, 3 (failed) |
| go-gc-tuned-batch | 2, 0, true, 0, 0 | 3, 0, true, 0, 2 |

What the unbound alloc-tests read:
- python-report-memo-bounded: both non-leak (earlier both inconclusive). os.rss voted with plateau and `no-growth`, through the noise floor; this is why refuted rose from 1 to 4.
- python-graph-churn: both non-leak. py.traced plateau; os.rss plateau with purge released (growth 4.9 and 5.8 MB, drop 9.3 and 10.3 MB). os.rss_file did not pass the first trend this time.
- go-gc-tuned-batch: one test, non-leak. No column passed the first trend, so go.heap_live decided (plateau, purge not-run).

Machine time of my runs: about 27 minutes. Evidence is in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-dla/f6814273-1d53-58fc-a01a-0b3a3a3915ac/scratchpad/u9chk-N1b/`: `replay-sweep.txt`, `replay-tests.txt`, `replay-detail.txt`, `replay-one.txt`, `replay-steps.txt`, `cmdlevel-summary.txt`, `scan-u8acc.txt`, `dyn/`, and the replay source in `replay/`.
unverified:
- The other nine of the twelve fixtures, and the refix report's counts for them.
- The seen-failing claims were checked by replaying each test's series against extracted copies of the code with one change removed, not by running the repository's tests on mutated source.
- The `go.heap_objects` `no-growth` path on a real run: the column did not pass the first trend in my go-gc-tuned-batch run.
- The os.rss_file exemption on a real run: os.rss_file did not pass the first trend in my python-graph-churn run, and its purge read `no-growth` in all 8 command-level runs.
- The sweep rates come from prepared series with uniform scatter; the rates on real programs are unknown.
- Workspace clippy returned from cache, so it was not re-checked from scratch. The Windows-gnu clippy and `test_grade.py` were not run; no file of this package is in those three crates.
- That the JVM purge steps move os.rss_file, and the per-kind statement for the C driver, shim and Rust: taken from the first check, by reading only.
- The skip of the Linux-only tests on macOS and Windows.
- How often the chance events recur on the runners.
